abstract: <jats:p>Chenopodium quinoa is a genetically diverse crop that can adapt to a wide range of environments, including temperatures and salinities. However, only a few studies have assessed the combined effects of two or more environmental factors on C. quinoa. Here, we investigated the effects of salinity (300 mM NaCl), elevated temperature (35 °C), and their interaction with growth, water–salt balance, the efficiency of photosystem II (PSII), the activity of cyclic electron transport (CET) around photosystem I (PSI), Rubisco and PEPC enzyme content, and the expression of photosynthetic genes. We found that elevated temperature did not decrease the biomass but caused a significant increase in the water and potassium content of C. quinoa leaves. The decrease in PSII efficiency under elevated temperature was accompanied by an increase in the expression of genes encoding the components of PSII (psbA) and linear electron transport (FDI), as well as the main photosynthetic protein Rubisco (rbcL). Moreover, the strongest effect was induced by the combined effect of elevated temperature and salinity, which induced high oxidative stress (a threefold increase in MDA), a threefold decrease in the biomass, a twofold decrease in PSII efficiency, and a two- to eightfold decrease in the expression of the photosynthetic genes psbA, FDI, and rbcL. PSI was more tolerant to all forms of stress; however, the combined effect of elevated temperature and salinity downregulated the expression of PGR5 and FNR1, which may diminish the role of PGR5/PGRL1-dependent CET in favor of the NDH-dependent CET of PSI. The obtained data on the functioning of photosystems and the expression of photosynthetic genes under combined stress (elevated temperature and salinity) can make a significant contribution to understanding the mechanisms of tolerance of C. quinoa to multiple stresses under climate change conditions.</jats:p>
title: Impact of Salinity, Elevated Temperature, and Their Interaction with the Photosynthetic Efficiency of Halophyte Crop Chenopodium quinoa Willd

abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Long-term exposure to dietary xenobiotics can induce oxidative stress in the gastrointestinal tract, possibly causing DNA damage and contributing to the initiation of carcinogenesis. Halophytes are exposed to constant abiotic stresses, which are believed to promote the accumulation of antioxidant metabolites like polyphenols. The aim of this study was to evaluate the antioxidant and antigenotoxic properties of the ethanol extract of the aerial part of the halophyte <jats:italic>Polygonum maritimum</jats:italic> L. (PME), which can represent a dietary source of bioactive compounds with potential to attenuate oxidative stress-related damage. The PME exhibited a high antioxidant potential, revealed by the in vitro capacity to scavenge the free radical DPPH (IC<jats:sub>50</jats:sub> = 2.29 ± 0.10 μg/mL) and the improved viability of the yeast <jats:italic>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</jats:italic> under oxidative stress (<jats:italic>p</jats:italic> < 0.001, 10 min). An antigenotoxic effect of PME against H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>-induced oxidative stress was found in <jats:italic>S. cerevisiae</jats:italic> (<jats:italic>p</jats:italic> < 0.05) with the dominant deletion assay. In vitro colorimetric assays and LC-DAD-ESI/MS<jats:sup>n</jats:sup> analysis showed that PME is a polyphenol-rich extract composed of catechin, (epi)catechin dimer and trimers, quercetin and myricetin glycosides. Hence, <jats:italic>P. maritimum</jats:italic> is a source of antioxidant and antigenotoxic metabolites for application in industries that develop products to provide health benefits.</jats:p>
title: Antigenotoxic properties of the halophyte Polygonum maritimum L. highlight its potential to mitigate oxidative stress-related damage

abstract: <jats:p>Halophytic plant resources play a vital role in meeting the needs of local people, and they have potential applications in nutrition and sustainable agriculture. Ethnobotanical surveys were conducted on foredunes at 41 study sites in 8 provinces of the south-central coastal region of Vietnam. The findings show that the majority of halophytic plants fall into the following resource groups: traditional medicine (45.13%, 88 species), food, (13.85%, 27 species), woody plants (4.62%, 9 species), and ornamentals (4.10%, 8 species). In comparison, 26.67% (54 species) have not been documented for specific uses. Halophytic resources account for 73.34% of the surveyed species, highlighting their significant ethnobotanical value. Cultivating these natural resources can benefit coastal communities by supporting local socio-economic development while promoting the environmental sustainability of the coastal soils and climate.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Aim and Objective:</jats:title>
<jats:p>urrently, the use of ingredients from natural sources has gained
great attention in the cosmetic field, especially for the development of new photoprotective
formulations. Therefore, the present study aimed to evaluate the cosmetic potential of the crude
methanol extract and the ethyl acetate fraction of the medicinal halophyte Tamarix gallica L. (Tg)
growing in the area of Tebessa in the eastern part of Algeria, by assessing their phenolic and
flavonoid contents, photoprotective and antioxidant activities.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
<jats:p> The research approach consisted of determination phenolic and flavonoid contents of aerial parts via FolinCiocalteu and aluminum chloride methods respectively. The antioxidant activity was measured through two in vitro methods
DPPH radical scavenging activity and total antioxidant capacity test (TAC). The in vitro photoprotective effect was
performed according to the parameter SPF (Sun Protection Factor) by using UV spectroscopic method in UV-B region
(290-320 nm).</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
<jats:p> The methanol extract (Tg-MeOH) and ethyl acetate (Tg-EtOAc) fraction showed good
antioxidant activity with IC<jats:sub>50</jats:sub> values of 14.05±0.66, 27.58±1.98 μg/mL respectively in the DPPH
test. Furthermore, both extracts displayed strong total antioxidant capacity (287.01±7.85,
246.7±1.12 mg AAE/g, respectively) in the TAC test. Both extracts exhibited high photoprotective
activity, with sun protection factor (SPF) values 37.03±0.22 and 36.08±0.03. The antioxidant and
photoprotective activities of these extracts were probably related to polyphenols content
(190.27±0.74 mg AGE /g and 121.77±1.29 mg AGE /g, respectively) and flavonoids (78.75±0.06
mg QE /g and 58.67±1.19mg/g).</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
<jats:p>Our finding show that extracts of Tamarix gallica L could be a promising source to be mixed as natural
sunscreens and antioxidants agent into photoprotective cosmetic formulations. </jats:p>
</jats:sec>
title: The Cosmetic Potential of The Medicinal Halophyte Tamarix Gallica L. (Tamaricaceae) Growing in The Eastern Part of Algeria: Photoprotective and Antioxidant Activities

project-description.description:
The global natural antioxidants market is expected to reach USD 4.14 billion by 2022, according to a new study by Grand View Research, Inc. The natural antioxidants market size has grown due to the increase of demand for natural antioxidants in food, cosmetics and pharmaceutical. The growing increase of consumer awareness regarding the benefits of natural oxidants incorporated in food and cosmetic products has driven this market. This growth has been mainly attributed to the increasing demand and consumption of processed foods, where food antioxidants are highly used to improve their shelf life. These antioxidants have also been added in cosmetic products to help skin protection from sun exposure roughness and ultraviolet induced skin cancer.
Currently, great interest has been focused on using natural antioxidants in food products, due to studies indicating adverse effects caused by synthetic antioxidants, such as allergies, gastrointestinal tract problems and in some cases the increased risk of cancer. There is a constant search for strategies to increase food products’ overall qualities and shelf life, in many cases by reducing or inhibiting oxidative damage; so the incorporation of antioxidants is one of the strategies to delay the oxidation of biomolecules. Antioxidants obtained from natural sources, possess great potential to be used as preservatives, replacing synthetic antioxidants. Therefore, the constant development in the field of natural ingredients is necessary, and exploratory studies carried out are important to identify and evaluate the isolated bioactive compounds from different plants, obtained through extraction technologies.

O mercado global de antioxidantes em 2022 poderá valer até 4.14 mil milhões de dólares, segundo Grand View research. O valor de mercado dos compostos antioxidantes tem vindo a crescer devido ao aumento da procura destes compostos para utilizações nas indústrias alimentares, farmacêuticas e cosmética. O aumento da consciencialização dos consumidores relativamente aos benefícios da incorporação destes compostos em alimentos e cosméticos tem vindo também a acelerar este crescimento. Esse crescimento tem sido atribuído principalmente ao aumento do consumo de alimentos processados, onde os antioxidantes alimentares são muito utilizados para melhorar sua vida útil. Estes antioxidantes têm sido também adicionados em produtos cosméticos para conferir proteção à pele contra os danos da exposição solar e cancro causado pelo excesso de luz UV.
De momento, o maior interesse tem sido focado na utilização de antioxidantes naturais em produtos alimentares, devido a alegações de efeitos adversos causados por antioxidantes sintéticos, tais como alergias, problemas do trato gastrointestinal e o aumento do risco de cancro. Estratégias que visem melhorar as qualidades de um produto alimentar e a sua vida útil, que em muitos casos se atinge através da redução ou inibição dos danos oxidativos; assim, a incorporação de antioxidantes é um dos alvos para retardar a oxidação de biomoléculas. Antioxidantes obtidos de fontes naturais apresentam um grande potencial como conservantes, substituindo assim as suas alternativas sintéticas. Deste modo, é necessário um constante desenvolvimento na área dos ingredientes naturais, e estudos exploratórios são importantes para identificar e avaliar estes compostos bioativos isoladamente obtidos através de tecnologias de extração.

abstract: <jats:p>Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase (PEPC) plays pivotal roles in the carbon fixation of photosynthesis and a variety of metabolic and stress pathways. <jats:italic>Suaeda aralocaspica</jats:italic> belongs to a single-cellular C<jats:sub>4</jats:sub> species and carries out a photosynthetic pathway in an unusually elongated chlorenchyma cell, which is expected to have PEPCs with different characteristics. To identify the different isoforms of <jats:italic>PEPC</jats:italic> genes in <jats:italic>S. aralocaspica</jats:italic> and comparatively analyze their expression and regulation patterns as well as the biochemical and enzymatic properties in this study, we characterized a bacterial-type PEPC (BTPC; SaPEPC-4) in addition to the two plant-type PEPCs (PTPCs; SaPEPC-1 and SaPEPC-2) using a genome-wide identification. <jats:italic>SaPEPC-4</jats:italic> presented a lower expression level in all test combinations with an unknown function; two SaPTPCs showed distinct subcellular localizations and different spatiotemporal expression patterns but positively responded to abiotic stresses. Compared to <jats:italic>SaPEPC-2</jats:italic>, the expression of <jats:italic>SaPEPC-1</jats:italic> specifically in chlorenchyma cell tissues was much more active with the progression of development and under various stresses, particularly sensitive to light, implying the involvement of <jats:italic>SaPEPC-1</jats:italic> in a C<jats:sub>4</jats:sub> photosynthetic pathway. In contrast, <jats:italic>SaPEPC-2</jats:italic> was more like a non-photosynthetic PEPC. The expression trends of two SaPTPCs in response to light, development, and abiotic stresses were also matched with the changes in PEPC activity <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic> (native) or <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic> (recombinant), and the biochemical properties of the two recombinant SaPTPCs were similar in response to various effectors while the catalytic efficiency, substrate affinity, and enzyme activity of SaPEPC-2 were higher than that of SaPEPC-1 <jats:italic>in vitro.</jats:italic> All the different properties between these two SaPTPCs might be involved in transcriptional (e.g., specific <jats:italic>cis</jats:italic>-elements), posttranscriptional [e.g., 5′-untranslated region (5′-UTR) secondary structure], or translational (e.g., PEPC phosphorylation/dephosphorylation) regulatory events. The comparative studies on the different isoforms of the PEPC gene family in <jats:italic>S. aralocaspica</jats:italic> may help to decipher their exact role in C<jats:sub>4</jats:sub> photosynthesis, plant growth/development, and stress resistance.</jats:p>
title: Genome-Wide Identification and Analysis of the Phosphoenolpyruvate Carboxylase Gene Family in Suaeda aralocaspica, an Annual Halophyte With Single-Cellular C4 Anatomy

abstract: <jats:p>A Gram-negative, non-spore-forming, endophytic bacterium, strain YC6886<jats:sup>T</jats:sup>, was isolated from the root of a halophyte,<jats:italic>Rosa rugosa</jats:italic>, which inhabits coastal areas of Namhae Island off the southern coast of Korea. Cells were non-motile, obligately aerobic rods and formed pale-yellow colonies. The isolate grew at 4–32 °C (optimum 25–28 °C) and at pH 6.5–9.5 (optimum pH 7.5) and grew optimally with 2–3 % (w/v) NaCl, but NaCl was not an absolute requirement for growth. Strain YC6886<jats:sup>T</jats:sup>produced yellow carotenoid pigments. Strain YC6886<jats:sup>T</jats:sup>exhibited the highest 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity with<jats:italic>Haloferula sargassicola</jats:italic>MN1-1037<jats:sup>T</jats:sup>(97.4 %). Sequence similarities between strain YC6886<jats:sup>T</jats:sup>and other members of the genus<jats:italic>Haloferula</jats:italic>were 93.9–94.7 %. DNA–DNA relatedness between strain YC6886<jats:sup>T</jats:sup>and<jats:italic>H. sargassicola</jats:italic>KCTC 22202<jats:sup>T</jats:sup>and<jats:italic>Haloferula rosea</jats:italic>KCTC 22201<jats:sup>T</jats:sup>was 27 and 15 %, respectively. The major fatty acids were iso-C<jats:sub>14 : 0</jats:sub>, C<jats:sub>16 : 0</jats:sub>and C<jats:sub>16 : 1</jats:sub>ω9<jats:italic>c</jats:italic>and minor components were C<jats:sub>14 : 0</jats:sub>, C<jats:sub>18 : 0</jats:sub>and anteiso-C<jats:sub>15 : 0</jats:sub>. The major respiratory quinone was menaquinone 9 and the DNA G+C content was 58.5 mol%. The polar lipid profile was composed of diphosphatidylglycerol, phosphatidylethanolamine, phosphatidylglycerol, an unknown phospholipid and an unknown phosphoglycolipid. On the basis of phenotypic, chemotaxonomic, DNA–DNA hybridization and phylogenetic analysis, strain YC6886<jats:sup>T</jats:sup>represents a novel species in the genus<jats:italic>Haloferula</jats:italic>, for which the name<jats:italic>Haloferula luteola</jats:italic>sp. nov. is proposed. The type strain is YC6886<jats:sup>T</jats:sup>( = KCTC 22447<jats:sup>T</jats:sup> = DSM 21608<jats:sup>T</jats:sup>). An emended description of the genus<jats:italic>Haloferula</jats:italic>is also presented.</jats:p>
title: Haloferula luteola sp. nov., an endophytic bacterium isolated from the root of a halophyte, Rosa rugosa, and emended description of the genus Haloferula
